definition: Job satisfaction is the degree to which a person feels positively about their work and work situation. In the source packet, it is treated as an important indicator of the quality of university teachers’ work and is influenced by factors such as work values, social support, and aspects of personal relationships.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence (“the degree to which a person feels positively about their work and work situation”) is not explicitly stated in the packet text; the packet discusses job satisfaction as a critical factor and measures/associations but does not provide this definitional wording.

The definition adds that job satisfaction is “influenced by factors such as … aspects of personal relationships.” The packet supports marital relationship effects (personal relationships), but it does not frame this as a general “aspects of personal relationships” influence beyond marital relationship; the wording is broader than what is directly supported.

The opening gloss generalizes job satisfaction as “the degree to which a person feels positively about their work and work situation,” but the packet only supports job satisfaction as a measure/factor used to estimate the quality of university teachers’ work; it does not define the term that broadly.
“Work situation” is not supported in the packet, which focuses on university teachers’ job satisfaction and related factors in that study context.
The definition should stay within the packet’s scope and not present a broader standalone definition as if it were established from the source.
